Q: Laravel batch jobs stuck in horizon A:

Got the same issue. Solved by adding \Illuminate\Queue\InteractsWithQueue trait. Batch processing calls release() on every job and its only available via trait

Q: Can't add AWS amplify ANAME to freenom domain DNS A:

I got same issue with the root domain in All-Inkl (no ANAME support). I solved it this way:

1. created www. subdomain with CNAME -> amplify
2. configured the root domain to redirect via 'permanently moved' to -> https://www.YOURDOMAIN.com

I guess this should be supported by all hosts. Browsers does not even show the 'www.', so seems fine for me.

Q: How to include <cuda_runtime.h> in .cpp file A:

For VS Code users , follow this :

1. Open the Command Palette (Ctrl+Shift+P), type "C/C++: Edit Configurations (UI)" and select it.

2. This opens the C/C++ Configurations file, scroll down and find the include path (includePath) section.

3. Add the directory containing cuda_runtime.h to the list in include path. This is :

For linux/mac :- /usr/local/cuda/include
For windows :- C:\\Program Files\\NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit\\CUDA\\v[version]\\include replace [version] with your installed version, e.g., v12.5

Q: How to keep Android app running after it is removed from the recent tasks list? A:

Yes, but you cannot guarantee it on modern Android. When the user removes the app from the recent tasks list, Android may stop your activities and sometimes your process as well. The recommended way to keep work running is a foreground service with a persistent notification.

If you need to react when the task is removed, override onTaskRemoved() in your service:

override fun onTaskRemoved(rootIntent: Intent?) {
    // handle cleanup or restart service
}

You can also set in the manifest:

<service
    android:name=".MyService"
    android:stopWithTask="false" />

However, Android background restrictions mean the system may still stop your app, so the recommended modern approach is to use:

  • ForegroundService for continuous work

  • WorkManager for scheduled/background tasks.

In short: you can't reliably keep an app running after it is swiped away unless it uses a foreground service designed for long-running work.

Q: Restore NuGet Packages from a Private Feed when building Docker Containers A:

After facing the same problem, I have looked around and there are couple of approaches.

1. dotnet nuget add source

Mentioned in this SO post.

However in order for Docker to correctly connect to a feed, you'd need to provide access token in that command, which is not practical.

2. nuget.config with creds

Define nuget.config file with private nuget feed source. Then add in Dockerfile command to copy that config file. THen nuget restore should work.

However, again in order for Docker to authorize with the feed, you'd need to put your credentials in nuget.config file. Still - not practical as you have to store credentials in plain text.

3. nuget.config without creds with autmatic nuget auth

As detailsed in Managing NuGet Credentials in Docker Scenarios, you can use nuget.config file, without storing creds there.

For that, you need to use Nuget authenticator + use credentials provider:

for creds provider you need to add in Dockerfile

RUN curl -L https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Microsoft/artifacts-credprovider/master/helpers/installcredprovider.sh  | sh

and in Azure Pipelines you'd need to add task Nuget Authenticate to provide nuget feed token.

However the documentation is not complete and example given there does not work fully, so I have workaround for that

parameters:
  - name: acrServer
    type: string
  - name: containerRepository
    type: string
  - name: dockerfile
    type: string
  - name: buildContext
    type: string
  - name: dockerRegistryServiceConnection
    type: string
  - name: tags
    type: object # array
    default: []
  - name: push
    type: boolean

steps:
  - task: NuGetAuthenticate@1
    name: NuGetAuthenticate
    displayName: "Authenticate with NuGet feed"

  - task: Docker@2
    displayName: Login to ACR
    inputs:
      containerRegistry: ${{ parameters.dockerRegistryServiceConnection }}
      command: login

  - script: |
      # Build array of full image URLs
      IMAGE_URLS=()
      for tag in ${{ join(' ', parameters.tags) }}; do
        IMAGE_URLS+=("${{ parameters.acrServer }}/${{ parameters.containerRepository }}:$tag")
      done

      # Build docker build arguments
      BUILD_ARGS=""
      for image_url in "${IMAGE_URLS[@]}"; do
        BUILD_ARGS="$BUILD_ARGS -t $image_url"
      done

      docker build \
        --build-arg FEED_ACCESSTOKEN="$FEED_ACCESSTOKEN" \
        $BUILD_ARGS \
        -f ${{ parameters.dockerfile }} \
        ${{ parameters.buildContext }}

      # Push all images (if push is enabled)
      if [ "${{ parameters.push }}" == "True" ]; then
        for image_url in "${IMAGE_URLS[@]}"; do
          echo "Pushing image: $image_url"
          docker push "$image_url"
        done
      else
        echo "Push disabled - only building images"
      fi
    displayName: Build and Push to ACR
    env:
      FEED_ACCESSTOKEN: $(VSS_NUGET_ACCESSTOKEN) # secret mapped here, not as parameter

I have also started github discussion on that.

Q: Can put 2 kernels into my os and a windows subsystem? A:

No. An operating system normally has only one kernel controlling the hardware. Two independent kernels cannot safely run on the same machine at the same time unless one of them runs inside a virtual machine or hypervisor.

Systems like Windows Subsystem for Linux don’t add a second kernel to Windows. In WSL1, Linux system calls are translated to the Windows kernel, and in WSL2 a real Linux kernel runs inside a lightweight virtual machine managed by Windows.

If you want Linux apps or a “Windows subsystem” in your OS, the typical approaches are:

  • Implement a compatibility layer (translate syscalls like WSL1).

  • Run the other OS in a VM.

  • Or implement a user-space subsystem on top of your kernel.

But you cannot just include two full kernels controlling hardware simultaneously in a normal OS design.

Q: VBA "Method 'Range' of object: '_worksheet' failed" when attempting to copy cells from one worksheet to another A:

Copy Data (Last Row)

Issues

  • No matter what, the line lastcopyRow = sourceSheet.Range("J2:J" & Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row yields lastcopyRow = 1 (which is wrong). Yielding lastcopyRow = 0 could be possible if you had a typo, e.g., lastcopiRow = sourceSheet.Range("J2:J" & Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row (note copi vs copy) which would also mean that you're not using Option Explicit (otherwise, there would be Compile error: Variable not defined) resulting in Run-time error '1004': Method 'Range' of object '_Worksheet' failed.

  • lastdestinationRow = Range("A:E" & Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row will raise a similar error Run-time error '1004': Method 'Range' of object '_Global' failed (note _Global vs _Worksheet) since it is missing an integer between A and : (wrong), or only one column should be used (correct).

Fix

  • Use Option Explicit at the top of each module to avoid loosing time over typos (it forces you to declare all variables).
  • Either determine which column has data in all rows to use it with the End property to calculate the 'last row', or use the Find method instead.

End

Option Explicit

Sub UpdateQCLog()
    
    ' Workbook
    Dim wb As Workbook: Set wb = ThisWorkbook ' workbook containing this code
    
    ' Source
    Dim sws As Worksheet: Set sws = wb.Sheets("QC Production Live Log Import")
    Dim slRow As Long: slRow = sws.Range("J" & sws.Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row
    Dim srg As Range: Set srg = sws.Range("J2:N" & slRow)
    
    ' Destination
    Dim dws As Worksheet: Set dws = wb.Sheets("% Yield by Product")
    Dim dlRow As Long: dlRow = dws.Range("A" & dws.Rows.Count).End(xlUp).Row
    Dim dcell As Range: Set dcell = dws.Range("A" & dlRow + 1)
    
    ' Copy.
    srg.Copy
    dcell.PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteValuesAndNumberFormats
    Application.CutCopyMode = False
    
    ' Select the first destination cell.
    'Application.Goto dcell
    
    ' Inform.
    MsgBox "QCLog updated.", vbInformation

End Sub

Find

Sub UpdateQCLogFind()
    
    ' Workbook
    Dim wb As Workbook: Set wb = ThisWorkbook ' workbook containing this code
    
    ' Source
    Dim sws As Worksheet: Set sws = wb.Sheets("QC Production Live Log Import")
    Dim srg As Range, slcell As Range
    With sws.Range("J2:N" & sws.Rows.Count)
        Set slcell = .Find(What:="*", After:=.Cells(1), LookIn:=xlFormulas, _
            SearchOrder:=xlByRows, SearchDirection:=xlPrevious)
        If slcell Is Nothing Then Exit Sub ' no data
        Set srg = .Resize(slcell.Row - .Row + 1)
    End With
    
    ' Destination
    Dim dws As Worksheet: Set dws = wb.Sheets("% Yield by Product")
    Dim drg As Range, dlcell As Range
    With dws.Range("A2:E" & dws.Rows.Count)
        Set dlcell = .Find(What:="*", After:=.Cells(1), LookIn:=xlFormulas, _
            SearchOrder:=xlByRows, SearchDirection:=xlPrevious)
        If dlcell Is Nothing Then ' no data; use first row
            Set drg = .Rows(1)
        Else ' existing data; use next row
            Set drg = .EntireColumn.Rows(dlcell.Row + 1)
        End If
    End With
    
    ' Copy.
    srg.Copy
    drg.PasteSpecial Paste:=xlPasteValuesAndNumberFormats
    Application.CutCopyMode = False
    
    ' Select the first destination cell.
    'Application.Goto drg.Cells(1)
    
    ' Inform.
    MsgBox "QCLog updated.", vbInformation

End Sub
